html:
A Chinese draft bank founded in about 1823 in Pingyao, Shanxi province, under the Qing dynasty. It is held to be the first of the piaohao, the Shanxi banks that moved money across China.

It grew out of a dye shop. Its owner, Li Daquan, and manager Lei Lütai saw that merchants carrying silver over long distances risked robbery. Instead, a merchant could pay silver at one branch and receive a draft, a paper order to pay, that another branch would cash in a distant city. Secret codes and seals protected the drafts.

The idea spread fast. Other Shanxi families copied it, and at their height the piaohao had branches in most big Chinese cities and handled much of the government's remittances of tax. They declined after the Taiping wars, the rise of foreign banks such as HSBC and the fall of the Qing in 1912, and Rishengchang closed in the 1930s. Its old building in Pingyao is now a museum.
